knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5.5)

## What this document does

It reads the stock symbols in `portfolio.txt`, downloads their daily prices from Yahoo Finance, calculates the mean, median, mode, standard deviation and a 50-day moving average of the close price, and shows the data in tables and charts. The functions are stored in `stock_functions.R` and `stock_display.R`.

## 1. Load packages and functions

```{r packages}
source("stock_functions.R")
setup_packages()          # installs quantmod, TTR and ggplot2 when they are missing
source("stock_display.R")
```

## 2. Symbols in the portfolio

```{r symbols}
get_symbols_from_file("portfolio.txt")
```

## 3. Import the data

```{r import}
stocks <- load_stock_data("portfolio.txt", from = "2024-01-01")
sapply(stocks, nrow)     # number of trading days per stock
```

## 4. Display the data

```{r display}
show_all(stocks, rows = 5)
```

## 5. Statistics

```{r stats}
res <- calculate_all_statistics(stocks, window = 50)
knitr::kable(res$summary, digits = 2, caption = "Close price statistics")
```

## 6. Charts

```{r ma}
chart_ma(res$detail, window = 50)
```

```{r returns}
chart_returns(res$detail)
```

```{r spread}
chart_spread(res$detail)
```

```{r variation}
chart_stats(res$summary)
```

## Notes

- Yahoo Finance data is downloaded with `quantmod::getSymbols()`, so internet access is required.
- The mode is calculated on prices rounded to 2 decimals because exact repeats are uncommon.
